text:
sam: Quick question — we keep seeing user identifiers in OTLP span attributes (user.id, email) from a handful of SDKs. Need a recommended approach for export-time handling to satisfy audits: do we pseudonymize in the collector, encrypt in the exporter, or block those attributes entirely?

ava: Prefer collector-side pseudonymization + audit bucket for raw. Reasons: consistent across exporters, easier to enforce retention, and we can rotate keys via KMS.

maria: Curious about scope — collector pseudonymization still allows cross-customer correlation if keys are shared. If we HMAC user.id with a tenant-specific key that's rotated, we should be fine. Do we have tenant-scoped keys?

linh: We don't today. But we could derive per-tenant HMAC keys from a master in KMS (HKDF). That avoids creating many KMS keys. Must document rotation semantics: old hashes remain valid for matching until rotation window ends.

sam: Two follow-ups: 1) how do we audit access to raw values when compliance requests them (legal/escalation)? 2) UX: how would this look in Console for engineers who need to debug?

ava: For audits we proposed an "ephemeral raw bucket" flow: collector writes encrypted raw spans to a secure S3 bucket with strict ACLs + object-level audit logs. Access requires approval & a signed short-lived decryption token issued by an audit service. That token usage is logged.

linh: Audit flow idea: sample 0.1% of raw spans for debugging signals automatically, but capture a manual "pull" flow where a user can flag a trace id in Console and request raw reveal (approval step). This avoids storing everything decrypted by default.

maria: We need to ensure retention policies are enforced server-side. Nothing should rely on client SDKs to drop attributes. Collector must apply attribute removal/pseudonymization before persistence and before exporting to third-party exporters.

ops-bot: config-change: telemetry.collector.pii_mode -> {strict|pseudonymize|scrub}. Canary set to pseudonymize in us-west region.

sam: That config enum is good. What's the difference between pseudonymize and scrub in practice?

ava: pseudonymize = deterministic HMAC with per-tenant salt stored in KMS, scrub = remove attribute entirely (replace with "[REDACTED]"). Also add "telemetry.metadata_only" label for spans allowed to contain non-identifiable info.

linh: Implementation note: do not use naive MD5; use HMAC-SHA256 with key rotation and store key version in span attribute like telemetry.pii_key_v=3 so we can re-identify in audit flow if permitted.

sam: Ok. For exporters to third-parties (Datadog, Honeycomb) do we export pseudonymized spans or scrubbed? We should default to pseudonymize but let orgs opt into scrubbed exports via policy.

maria: Agreed. Also add a per-tenant policy that prevents export of raw/hashed IDs outside the org: exporter.policy.block_raw_identifiers=true. Default deny for external exporters.

linh: Console UX: show a little shield icon next to spans that had pii attributes removed or pseudonymized; allow "request raw" which opens a modal with ROI/approval flow and links to the audit ticket. For canary we can show a banner: "Pseudonymization active (us-west)".

sam: Nice. What about sampling for audit retention? We don't want to keep raw forever but need searchable audit trails for 90 days per compliance.

ava: Plan: keep pseudonymized spans in main index indefinitely (or per tenant retention), keep encrypted raw objects for 90 days in an audit bucket; access requires the audit service and operator approval; then auto-delete after retention window. All deletions logged to the audit trail.

telemetry-bot: canary-report: pseudonymize rollout (us-west) — 3k spans/day affected, no exporter errors observed.

maria: Encryption at rest for the audit bucket is mandatory. Also require object-level SSE-KMS with a separate audit KMS key. Operators cannot decrypt with their own KMS privileges; only the audit service can.

linh: Also consider adding a "lightweight fingerprint" attribute: telemetry.fingerprint = truncated-HMAC(user.id, 64bits). Allows dedupe for rate-limiting and correlations without full identifier. Document collision probability.

sam: Can we provide a config example for collector?

ava: Posted snippet: 
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  pii_filter:
    mode: pseudonymize
    attributes:
      - key: user.id
        action: hmac
        key_ref: kms://projects/…/locations/global/keyRings/telemetry/cryptoKeys/tenant-derived
    add_attribute: { telemetry.pii_key_v: "3" }
exporters:
  otlp/common:
    endpoint: internal-ingest:4317
```

linh: Minor: ensure the exporter pipeline tags spans with export_policy=internal_only or external_allowed to block misrouted exporters at runtime. Also add a debug flag to emit pseudo->real map to audit logs only (never to regular logs).

maria: Legal also asked about ability to show proof-of-deletion. We should record a signed deletion manifest listing object ids and KMS key versions and store that manifest immutably (write-once) for compliance checks.

sam: Sounds good. Final question: performance impact? HMAC per-span adds CPU. Any numbers?

linh: Rough bench on a c6i-large-ish collector: HMAC-SHA256 adds ~5-8% CPU at 50k spans/s if implemented in native code path and batched. We should default-enable on dedicated pipelines and make it opt-in for low-tier hosted customers.

ava: We'll draft a runbook: config enum, collector PR with HMAC impl, audit bucket + audit service design, Console wire for request/approval flow, and a rollout plan: dev -> canary -> region-wide, with metrics (span drop rates, exporter errors, approval latency).

sam: Thanks — please add owners and put a brief spec in eng-platform RFC board. I'll open the RFC and ping privacy/legal. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: rfc created: RFC-telemetry-pseudonymization-2026 tracked by sam, ava, linh (link: internal/rfcs/telemetry-pseudonymization-2026)

telemetry-bot: nightly-alert: pseudo-rollout health ok, no anomalies.
